reason: The mechanism is real, but the subject and scope are wrong. No 'search-tier plugin' exists: the Exa/R7-R8 search lanes are dead (search-headers.ts:27-30) and the marketplace catalog has no search entry. The actual gap is that `remove()` on ANY credentialed non-broker plugin (e.g. vysted-news `plugin-secret:vysted-news:newsapi_key`) never calls deleteSecret. runtime.removePlugin only patches config and unloads, and disconnectBroker is broker-only and does not touch the keychain. Leaving the secret on `disable()` is correct: disable is reversible and the plugin stays installed. The legacy `plugin-secret:vysted-search-exa` orphan also has no migration that cleans it. The secret stays in the user's own OS keychain and is never exposed, so low.
evidence: src/store/marketplace.ts:25-45, src/store/marketplace.ts:176-208, src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:343-353, src/lib/marketplace.ts:135-160, src/lib/search-headers.ts:27-30, src/lib/keychain.ts:34
evidence_checked: Opened the marketplace store disable/remove/configure, plugin-runtime removePlugin, the catalog entries, the keychain namespaces and the search-headers dead-lane note.
repro_check: Read the remove() path: runtime.removePlugin -> patchConfig({installed:false}) + unloadPlugin. There is no deleteSecret/keychainDelete call, while configure() does call deleteSecret for emptied optional fields (marketplace.ts:227). So the removed plugin's secret survives.

reason: Partly true, but the headline overstates it. The static store default is 'ollama', yet a clean install opens OnboardingFlow. Its Cloud step validates and stores an OpenRouter key AND sets defaultProviderId='openrouter' plus the model, so the guided path does work out of the box. On a true clean install no funded key exists (BYOK), so the keyless local default is the local-first choice. What remains real: skipping onboarding, or adding the key later through Settings or `/key`, leaves the default on ollama. Only Settings 'Set default' and `/provider` flip it, so the user must switch lanes by hand after adding a key. That is a medium onboarding snag, not a high broken core flow.

repro_check: grep -rn setDefaultProviderId src -> OnboardingFlow.tsx:356 sets 'openrouter' after a validated key. The key-set path (ChatSidebar.tsx:724-732) only opens the key dialog and never changes the default.
